site_description: Portfolio of Prashray Nagar, an ASIC and FPGA design and verification engineer specializing in RTL, UVM, SoC integration, and computer architecture.

profile.name: Prashray Nagar
profile.title: ASIC/FPGA Design and Verification Engineer
profile.headline: ASIC and FPGA design and verification engineer focused on front-end RTL, reusable IP, functional verification, and computer architecture.
about: I am a computer engineer with a background in digital hardware design, verification, FPGA-based prototyping and computer architecture. I completed my Master of Computer Engineering at North Carolina State University, where I developed practical experience through engineering projects involving SystemVerilog, UVM, RTL development, hardware interfaces and architecture simulation. My work focuses on translating technical requirements into implementable designs, building reusable hardware components, developing systematic verification strategies and analysing results through simulation and testing.

Through my engineering internship and academic projects, I have worked with digital interfaces, peripheral IP, verification environments, processor architecture and performance analysis. I enjoy understanding why a design behaves as it does, identifying failure conditions and using evidence to improve reliability and performance. I am currently seeking a full-time engineering opportunity where I can contribute to hardware development, learn from experienced engineers and grow into increasingly complex design and verification responsibilities.
profile.resume_intro: Download a concise overview of my ASIC, FPGA, RTL, and verification experience.

bullets: Developed an RTL testbench mutation grader for agent-generated ASIC testbenches, defining targeted tests and debug heuristics that achieved more than 70% fault-detection accuracy across five production-representative IP-block scenarios.
Executed design, validation, and synthesis for an FPGA-based SoC prototype targeting an ASIC tape-out, structuring peripheral IP for portability between FPGA and ASIC flows.
Authored reusable UART, SPI, GPIO, and USB peripheral IP in Verilog and SystemVerilog; integrated the blocks into the SoC bus fabric and validated on-target operation before ASIC handoff.
Developed embedded hardware interfaces and firmware communication routines across distributed microcontrollers using SPI, I2C, and UART.
Configured RTOS tasks and low-latency interrupt handling for multi-sensor acquisition, synchronizing peripheral actuators with sub-100 ms response.
Engineered power-efficient controller nodes with embedded edge processing to reduce false alarms while operating within thermal and power limits.

projects.title: I2C Multi-Bus Verification Using Layered UVM
projects.description: Layered SystemVerilog UVM verification of a configurable I2C multi-bus controller with coverage-driven regressions.
projects.summary: A layered UVM environment for a configurable I2C multi-bus controller with Avalon-MM and Wishbone host interfaces.
projects.problem: Verify a configurable I2C Multi-Bus master controller across its host-side register interfaces and multi-master, multi-bus behavior. The environment needed reusable components, protocol-aware checking, and coverage feedback rather than a collection of directed tests.
work: Designed the controller integration around VHDL RTL with Avalon-MM and Wishbone interfaces for SoC use.
Built layered SystemVerilog UVM agents, sequencers, drivers, monitors, and a scoreboard.
Exercised multi-master and multi-bus behavior through modular sequences and automated regressions.
Connected assertions and functional coverage to expose missing protocol and configuration scenarios.
projects.result: 92% functional coverage with assertion-linked coverage analysis.
projects.result_detail: Reached 92% functional coverage through automated regression and assertion-linked coverage analysis.

projects.title: MESI and MOESI Cache-Coherence Simulator
projects.description: Cycle-accurate C++ simulation of MESI and MOESI coherence across a four-processor shared-memory system.
projects.summary: A trace-driven shared-memory simulator comparing MESI and MOESI coherence behavior under bus contention.
projects.problem: Measure how coherence policy affects bus traffic and transaction behavior in a symmetric multiprocessing system, particularly when dirty cache lines can be supplied by another cache instead of memory.
work: Developed a cycle-accurate, trace-driven shared-memory simulator for four processors.
Modeled snooping-based MESI and MOESI finite-state machines in C++.
Instrumented invalidation behavior, cache-to-cache transfers, memory transactions, and shared-bus arbitration.
Compared protocol behavior under parallel execution traces and identified contention sources.
projects.result: MOESI reduced memory-bus traffic by 13% through Owned-state cache-to-cache sharing.
projects.result_detail: MOESI reduced memory-bus traffic by 13% and lowered transaction latency by using the Owned state for cache-to-cache data sharing.

projects.title: Branch-Predictor Simulator for Execution-Trace Analysis
projects.description: C++ simulator comparing bimodal, gshare, and hybrid branch-prediction algorithms using processor traces.
projects.summary: A configurable C++ simulator for evaluating bimodal, gshare, and tournament branch predictors on execution traces.
projects.problem: Evaluate branch-prediction organizations and parameter choices that reduce mispredictions and pipeline flushes in a speculative superscalar processor.
work: Built a configurable C++ simulator for bimodal, gshare, and tournament/hybrid prediction.
Implemented pattern-history-table indexing, global-history updates, selector training, and predictor statistics.
Swept predictor configurations against processor execution traces to compare accuracy and storage tradeoffs.
Analyzed how history length and table sizing affected simulated pipeline stalls.
projects.result: Achieved 90% prediction accuracy and a one-percentage-point gain over the bimodal baseline.
projects.result_detail: Reached 90% prediction accuracy, improving by one percentage point over the bimodal baseline and reducing simulated pipeline stalls.
